newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajiks hold hostage U.N.,aide workers, journalists.
newsitem.headline: Tajiks hold hostage U.N.,aide workers, journalists.

text.p: A group of Tajik rebels which seized four U.N. observers earlier this week has detained several Russian reporters and two Red Cross workers who went to investigate the kidnapping, a U.N. spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We have radio contact with our people and we have information that four journalists have been detained," the spokesman said.

Russian news agencies identified the journalists as Suraye Sabirova of Interfax news agency, Galina Gridneva of Itar-Tass news agency, correspondent Adil Ashurov and cameraman Bobojon Tuganov of the commercial NTV television.
But RIA news agency said that NTV driver was also among the hostages.

The reporters had been planning to rendevous with an armed group led by Rizvon Sadirov, who once fought for the former Soviet republic's Islamic opposition against the secular government but whose loyalties now are unclear.

Sadirov's group on Tuesday captured the U.N. personnel, Austrian, Ukrainian and two Swiss military observers and an interpreter, about four km (two miles) from the town of Obigarm in the centre of the remote, mountainous republic.

The U.N. spokesman said a foreign employee of the International Red Cross and an interpreter bringing medical aid to one of the military observers were seized on Tuesday. He gave no further details as to the identity of the Red Cross workers.
The U.N. mission in Tajikistan issued a statement demanding "immediate and unconditional" release of all hostages.

A U.N. official in Dushanbe said that the mission was in constant radio contact with the hostages. "We haven't heard complains from them about bad treatment of any sort," said the official who refused to give his name.
Sadyrov's group is demanding safe passage for its members based in neighbouring Afghanistan back into the former Soviet republic.

The United Nations Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) has about 45 military personnel in the republic to observe a fragile peace agreement aimed at ending a bitter four-year civil war between the secular government and Islamist opposition forces.
A ceasefire agreed between the government and the guerrillas has held for nearly two months and further peace talks are due to be held on February 26 in Moscow.
Last December, Sadirov's group took 23 people hostage, including seven U.N. observers, to demand the release of his brother. All the hostages were later released.
